knowledge_point.title: Calculating Vertical Asymptotes With Common Factors in the Numerator and Denominator

question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors. Then, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x.$

Factoring the numerator and denominator and canceling any common factors, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x-1}{(x+2)(x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{x-1}}{(x+2)(\cancel{x-1})} \\  & =\frac{1}{x+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
x+2=0
$$

This gives the solution $x=-2.$

Therefore, the equation of the vertical asymptote is $x=-2.$

To find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors. Then, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x.$

Factoring the numerator and denominator and canceling any common factors, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x}{x(x-4)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{x}}{\cancel{x}(x-4)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
x-4=0
$$

This gives the solution $x=4$. Therefore, $x=4$ is the only vertical asymptote.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: The function has no vertical asymptotes

To find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors. Then, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x.$

Factoring the numerator and denominator and canceling any common factors, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{4x-1}{4{x}^{2}-21x+5} \\  & =\frac{4x-1}{(x-5)(4x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{4x-1}}{(x-5)\cancel{(4x-1)}} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
x-5=0
$$

This gives the solution $x=5.$

Therefore, the equation of the vertical asymptote is $x=5.$

To find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors. Then, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x.$

Factoring the numerator and denominator and canceling any common factors, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}+6x+8}{{x}^{2}+10x+24} \\  & =\frac{(x+2)(x+4)}{(x+6)(x+4)} \\  & =\frac{(x+2)\cancel{(x+4)}}{(x+6)\cancel{(x+4)}} \\  & =\frac{x+2}{x+6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
x+6=0
$$

This gives the solution $x=-6.$

Therefore, the equation of the vertical asymptote is $x=-6.$
